questions.q: In MCP's architecture, what is the MCP Host?
options: The physical server machine a company owns
A JSON file listing every available tool
The internet connection between a client and server
The AI application that coordinates and manages one or more MCP clients, such as Claude Desktop or Claude Code
questions.explain: The host is the application the person actually uses. It coordinates everything by creating and managing MCP client connections.

questions.q: If a host connects to three different MCP servers, how many MCP clients does it create?
options: Zero — clients are only needed for remote servers
One shared client used for all three connections
Three — one dedicated client per server connection
A number decided by the server, not the host
questions.explain: A host creates one dedicated client per server it connects to. Each client maintains its own independent connection to its corresponding server.

questions.q: What transport does a typical local MCP server use, and how many clients does it usually serve?
options: stdio; typically a single client, since it's tied to one running local process
Streamable HTTP; typically many clients
Email; an unlimited number of clients
Bluetooth; exactly two clients
questions.explain: Local servers run as a process on the same machine and communicate over stdio (standard input/output), which is inherently a one-process-to-one-process connection.

questions.q: What is the key difference between MCP's data layer and transport layer?
options: There is no difference — they are the same thing
The data layer defines the JSON-RPC 2.0 message protocol and core primitives; the transport layer defines how those messages physically move (e.g. stdio vs. Streamable HTTP)
The transport layer only exists for local servers
The data layer is optional and can be skipped
questions.explain: Keeping these separate lets the same JSON-RPC 2.0 message format work identically whether a server is local (stdio) or remote (Streamable HTTP) — the data layer doesn't need to know which transport carried its messages.

questions.q: A remote MCP server, like the official Sentry MCP server, typically uses which transport, and why does that matter for how many clients it can serve?
options: stdio; because stdio can serve unlimited remote clients
No transport is needed for remote servers
Streamable HTTP; because HTTP-based communication, like a normal web API, can serve many clients concurrently
USB; because MCP is physically a USB protocol
questions.explain: Remote servers use Streamable HTTP, which — like any HTTP-based API — can handle many concurrent client connections, unlike stdio's inherently single-process nature.
